Claire — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline, and I attached our one-page enterprise security checklist (see attachment). Monica (CS) and Marissa (Solutions) are looped in to own the implementation milestones and kickoffs.

Summary for Veridian’s security team:
- SSO/SAML: We support SAML 2.0 IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. We can ingest IdP metadata or configure manually. Typical turn-up time after metadata exchange: 1–3 business days for basic auth, 3–7 days for full attribute mapping + testing.
- SCIM: We provide SCIM 2.0 with configurable attribute mapping and bulk user sync. SCIM can be enabled in parallel with SAML but we recommend completing SAML first for auth testing.
- IP allowlists: Support both static CIDR allowlists and customer-managed reverse-proxy ingress (we can accept a set of CIDR ranges or work with static outbound NATs).
- Service accounts: We recommend creating dedicated service accounts for provisioning and automation; token lifetime policy configurable per org.
- Org policies & logging: Audit logs (admin actions, auth events, provisioning events) are retained by default 90 days; extended retention and KMS options available on private deployments.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Veridian to send SAML metadata + IdP admin contact.
2) Fill the SCIM attribute mapping spreadsheet (attached if helpful).
3) Agree on an IP allowlist mode and provide CIDR ranges (or confirm use of our dedicated egress).
4) Schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (IdP admin + CS + engineering).

Attaching: redwood-enterprise-security-checklist-v1.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber\Account Executive, Redwood Inference\jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122

Hi Claire — putting concrete dates against the items Jonas listed so your security and platform teams can plan. I’ve attached a working milestones workbook. Key asks from your side are bolded.

Proposed implementation milestones (pilot scope):
1) Metadata exchange & IdP access (Day 0–2) — Veridian provides SAML metadata XML and IdP admin contact.
2) Test SP config (Day 2–4) — Redwood configures SP, we validate IdP->SP login, capture SAML assertion attributes.
3) SCIM attribute mapping & first sync (Day 4–7) — Veridian completes the SCIM mapping csv; Redwood executes a scoped bulk sync and confirms group sync behavior.
4) IP allowlist & service account setup (Day 5–8) — Provide CIDRs or confirm static egress; designate service account names and intended permission scopes.
5) Cutover & smoke tests (Day 9–10) — validate MFA exemptions, session lengths, audit events in console.

Operational details / configuration defaults we will propose during kickoff:
- SAML attributes we commonly request: email, firstName, lastName, groups, entitlements.
- SCIM: we support user.active, user.displayName, user.emails[type=work], groups via membership relationship.
- Service accounts: token TTL default 90 days; recommend rotation schedule and an assigned owner (we can add reminders).
- Audit logs: default 90d retention; we can push logs to a customer-owned SIEM via secure connector for longer retention (add-on).

Please send the following so we can lock dates:
- SAML metadata XML (required)
- IdP admin contact (name + email + preferred time zone)
- SCIM attribute mapping CSV with your canonical attributes
- Any IP CIDRs you will require for allowlisting, or confirmation to use Redwood static egress IPs

Attachment: implementation-milestones.xlsx

If it helps, I can run the kickoff meeting and invite our infra engineer (service-owner for SAML/SCIM). Suggest 60-minute slot next week; what windows work for your IdP team?
